title: WTR1: wide top blocks with ramped triple-cap trees

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2N), the SAME fixed WTR1 configuration of proof.md recovers all of s with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal coset copies. It uses the five-control ramped tree with rounded triple cap, high-confidence exact-translation extraction, literal linear merges, TREE(D,B) with several unused top bits for the odd part, the charged stride grid/CRT decoder, original two-adic parity recovery, explicit pre-block source cap and deterministic aggregate work cap and finite exhaustive branch n<65536. All bounds hold jointly on EVERY branch including rejected copies, failed attempts, extraction errors and cutoff aborts. Total charged sequential work, including classical bit work, every address tariff, gates and complete uniform gate generation, source acquisition, decoder enumeration, setup and cleanup, is O(n^(15/4)2^(sqrt(2n))), enclosed by B_T=n^(15/4)2^(a sqrt(n)). Exact growth index1/2. Here a is the exact same u_333/v_333 rational as CS1, generated from (10,7) by (u,v)->(3u+4v,2u+3v), with u^2-2v^2=2. The complete value is in this structured bound. The proof establishes actual sqrt(2n) bounds first; a-sqrt(2) never absorbs a polynomial time factor.

For the SAME fixed WTR1 algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N>=2 and every s, the guaranteed malformed fraction is epsilon(n)=0. All acquired source copies must be independent ideal coset states. Under exactly this promise, unconditional full-secret recovery has probability at least 1-2^-8 > 2/3 jointly with the four all-branch resource bounds above. No positive corruption tolerance or impossibility of greater tolerance is asserted.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
